reading_status: frozen spontaneous reading after prose, before neutral questions
access_and_order_limitations: Listed stage2 names, then read instructions, commission and full story in one command. Viewed charts in numeric order after reading prose. No links followed and no outside sources or other stages accessed. Stage1 file not opened or modified.
story_understanding: The story narrows the negative-oil headline to one daily WTI spot benchmark at Cushing on 20 April 2020. Both WTI and Brent had already lost about 70 percent before this event. WTI alone among these two series went briefly negative, with positive weekly and monthly averages. The proposed explanation is that a physically delivered WTI futures contract was about to expire: holders unable to store the oil at Cushing accepted negative prices to escape taking delivery. The spot benchmark went negative on the same day. Brent also suffered severely, nearly reaching its series low the next day.
relationships_understood: Chart 1 compares the shared decline with WTI-specific negative pricing and the subsequent recovery. Chart 2 distinguishes the one-trading-day extreme from the positive weekly and monthly summaries. The prose distinguishes the EIA spot value of minus $36.98 from the better-known futures settlement of minus $37.63 and locates the explanatory account in a CFTC report rather than claiming that a price chart proves causality.
what_prose_adds_or_changes: The basic chart-first impression stands. The prose supplies the missing delivery/storage/expiry mechanism and geographical context, identifies the source and price concept, and gives a much longer historical comparison for the rarity of the WTI event. It adds that Brent nearly matched its historical low rather than simply remaining positive. COVID-19 lockdowns provide temporal context for the preceding broad decline, though the explanation concentrates on the negative day. It resolves my uncertainty about the incomplete chart-2 title by explicitly identifying that chart as WTI.
uncertainty_and_unanswered_questions: The causal paragraph explains trading in futures and then says the spot price went negative the same day. I still want the connecting step: how did the futures delivery squeeze set or transmit to this particular spot-price observation?

Storage scarcity is stated, but its scale and the reason storage had become scarce are not shown. The earlier shared collapse is situated during lockdowns without much explanation of demand or supply.
The text responsibly says the dataset cannot establish why Brent stayed positive, but the geographical contrast still encourages an untested explanation based on landlocked storage versus shipping.

The categorical opening that one benchmark went negative is qualified later by the admission that the dataset covers only two. I read it as one of these two, not proof that no other oil price was negative.
The claims about the full historical series and the CFTC account are additional prose evidence I have not verified.
The averaging treatment of missing/non-trading days is still unspecified.
presentation_observations: The main headline appears twice consecutively in the Markdown. Chart 2 still visibly starts with incomplete W spot price. Otherwise chart labels are readable, and prose gives clear references to their key comparisons.
